# Hello!
My name is Suraj Joshi. I’m a third-year medical student at the [Tufts University School of Medicine](https://medicine.tufts.edu) in Boston. 

I am interested in building a life that integrates academic and practical pursuits in 
- [Moral](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/moral-theory/)/Political Philosophy, 
- Medicine, 
- Computer Science and Digital/Computer Systems, and 
- Systems Theory.

My mission and values are described in [[दृष्टि|Values Declaration]] and [[Values Statement.pdf]]. 
My lifelong intellectual interests are described in [[Syllabus Vitae 02.27.2025.pdf]] and [[Curriculum Vitae Verus.pdf]]. 

# My approach
There are many ways to learn and do things. You can learn by following directions from a credentialed authority (the default model in education and medical school); you can learn on the internet; you can learn by talking to people; you can learn by trying things out yourself. 

I take a hybrid approach. When it comes to formal fields like philosophy and computer science/systems, I pay respect to the contributions of people way smarter and with much more free time than me. So I spend a good amount of time reading technical/contemporary books and trying to dissect them. Examples include my [[Annotation of The Sources of Normativity]] and [[Annotation of Computer Systems A Programmer's Perspective]]. The same goes for medicine: I basically accept the credentialed authority of medical doctors in the US, and believe that they have the skills and experience to train me to become one myself.

But I also try to implement and recreate things myself, especially when pre-established ways of doing things don’t fit well in my life or seem inefficient. An example is [[metapcms]], a “meta-degree” that tries to craft a personal “PhD” or advanced study program in the disciplines I describe in [[#Hello!]].
